theory.target: For transitive permutations A,B of d sheets and a closed walk B^n followed by A from x, test whether d can replace the local B-orbit length m in endpoint and winding calculations; identify the exact period and preserve the uniform-degree quantifier in the prior concentration lemma.
definitions: d>=1 sheets, permutations A and B, joint transitivity for connected actions; x is a base sheet and n>=0.
Read B n times then A; closure means A(B^n(x))=x. This is a cyclic rotation of ab^n.
m is the least positive B-return time of x, not the order of B or the total sheet count.
Winding counts complete traversals of the directed local B-cycle; time zero and the closing A-step are excluded.
A graph-simple certificate has n+1 distinct preclosure vertices; this is not a necessary test for surface simplicity.
delta(gamma) denotes minimum simple-lift degree; a uniform bound is one D for the whole selected family.
assumptions: A and B are bijections of {0,...,d-1}; together they act transitively.
Read a cyclic rotation of a*b^n starting immediately after the a-edge: apply B n times, then A; closure is A(B^n(x))=x.
n is a nonnegative integer; m is the least positive return time of x under B, not the order of B and not d.
A graph-simple witness visits n+1 distinct vertices before the closing A edge; this is sufficient for an embedded graph circle, not a necessary criterion for surface simplicity.
No ribbon-graph simplicity algorithm, surface lower-bound proof, hyperbolic three-manifold construction or parent-solution claim.
The topology of the cited curve family remains a primary-source dependency; the packet independently checks finite monodromy only.
approaches_considered: Substitute total degree for the local period based only on connectedness and closure; falsified by a three-sheet action.
Use local cycle coordinates and exact quotient/remainder, removing transitivity from the algebraic period lemma.
Independently rebuild literal paths and union-find connectivity; retain source topology as a separate proof dependency.
falsification_targets: Connected actions force a single B-cycle.
Pointwise finite degrees suffice for uniform finite pigeonhole.
Repeated graph vertices by themselves prove a curve is nonsimple on its surface.

claims.statement: Joint transitivity and closure of B^n A suffice to use total degree d as the local B period.
claims.falsification_condition: The exact A=[2,0,1],B=[1,0,2],x=0,n=5 certificate has d=3,m=2; endpoint and winding substitutions both fail.

claims.statement: For any two permutations, the local first-return period m gives endpoint B^(n mod m)(x) and floor(n/m) complete B-cycle traversals. Joint transitivity is unnecessary for this algebraic statement. Ordinary universal proof, not independently authored or kernel accepted.
claims.falsification_condition: A missed invertibility assumption, time-count convention or contradictory permutation case.

claims.statement: For n=0,...,16, cyclic successor permutations on n+1 sheets give connected graph-simple B^n A walks. Surface simplicity is not computed.
claims.falsification_condition: An invalid permutation, missing degree, failed closure or repeated preclosure vertex.

claims.statement: Two algorithms agree over 742417 rooted exponent cases from 15017 permutation pairs; 41244 closed walks fail degree-reduced endpoints and 44604 fail degree-based winding counts. All 65 aggregate rows match; seven corruptions are rejected.
claims.falsification_condition: Any omitted domain element, table mismatch or accepted corruption.

claims.statement: The primary source supplies a growing simple-lift lower bound for its specified family; its surface-topological proof remains an external dependency, not a computationally verified theorem here.

claims.statement: Pointwise finite simple-lift degrees do not supply the uniform degree hypothesis needed by the prior concentration argument. An unbounded family does not exclude a different infinite bounded-degree subfamily.
claims.falsification_condition: A swapped quantifier or an inference from worst-case growth to nonexistence of every bounded subfamily.
